subject: Intercept meaning in dummy factor model

messages.author: 399bf2e734c020dc
messages.subject: Intercept meaning in dummy factor model
parts:
Hi all,

I have a model that I built over a year ago, and for a reason I can no longer remember I followed the advice of another post in this group (possibly to help with identifiability?) I split the factor fixed effects into dummy 0/1 variables for each factor level. I then also have an intercept (specified =1) in the model. In this situation I am not sure what the intercept represents, if someone might know?

Here are my current thoughts

1. does it represent when all dummy variables are 0?
2. is it still a universal constant that is added to each dummy coefficient?
3. lastly, would it be recommended to remove in a model with a dummy factor variable?

Many thanks,
Sylvan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Intercept meaning in dummy factor model
parts:
1. Yes
2. It's not added to the coefficients. It's added to the combined effect predictor.
3. If the dummy variables are from a factor variable, so that they are never all 0 at the same time, you need to ensure identifiability in some way. One option is to not include an intercept. Another is to remove one of the dummy variables and use that factor level as a reference level.
Those options are exactly what happens mathematically with linear factor variable effects.
Finn
